units: Ber. 35ᵃ, a. e. כ׳ זית איקרי כ׳ סתמא לא אקרי an orchard of olive trees is called kerem zayith, but not plain kerem.
Ib. (ref. to Maas. Sh. V, 1 sq., a. fr.) חד תני כ׳ רבע … נטע רבעי one authority reads everywhere a kerem of the fourth year’s crop, the other nʾtʿa (plantation) &c.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32:1">Lev. R. s. 32</cite> (play on <cite ref="K01230"><he>כְּרֻם</he></cite>, <cite ref="Psalms 12:9">Ps. XII, 9</cite>) <he>כַּרְמָן של ממזרים</he> the plantation (genealogy, cmp. <cite ref="J00273"><he>יִחוּס</he></cite>) of the bastards.
Kil. IV, 1, v. קָרַחַת; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. circle of scholars, college, esp. כ׳ ביבנה the college of R. Johanan b. Zaccai in Jamnia (v. יַבְנֶה).

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 4:6">Keth. IV, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 131b">B. Bath. 131ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:33">Y. Ber. IV, 7ᵈ</cite> top; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Berakhot 63b:5">Ber. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ ביבנה</he> for which <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:5">Cant. R. to II, 5</cite>: <cite ref="A00918"><he>אוּשָׁא</he></cite>.]—Pl. <he>כְּרָמִים</he>.
Men. VIII, 6 (86ᵇ) כ׳ העבודים carefully cultivated vineyards (dug over twice a year); a. e.—בֵּית כֶּרֶם pr. n. pl. Beth-Kerem.
<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 2:7">Nidd. II, 7</cite> <he>בקעת ב׳ כ׳</he> the valley of Beth K. (whose soil was red); <cite ref="Tosefta Niddah 3:11">Tosef. ib. III, 11</cite>.
